caption: What if you jumped on other worlds? On Earth, a good jump lifts you about half a metre and you're back down in under a second. On the Moon, gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's, so the same jump takes you about 3 metres up and keeps you in the air for about 4 seconds. That's where India's Pragyan rover is parked. On Mars, gravity is about 38% of ours: roughly a 1.3 metre jump. Venus is almost the same as Earth, but the surface is about 465°C. Jupiter has no solid ground, and at its cloud tops gravity is about 2.4 times ours, so you'd manage a 20 cm hop. On Pluto you'd soar about 8 metres for around 10 seconds. The twist: comet 67P's escape speed is only about 1 m/s, so one jump would launch you into space. ESA's Philae lander bounced about 1 km high there in 2014. Where would YOU jump first? 👇
